source_snapshot.items: Test connections between BMC I2C-6 and UPHY1 from first PG548
source_snapshot.procedure: From BMC reads bus5 mux0x71, writes0x04 to select port2 and references PID1114953.
source_snapshot.criteria: Only generic collection language; no downstream address/reply, mux readback or restore value.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; invents physical probing/solder/photos instead of the supplied BMC functional path.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: Retains unsupported physical-only interpretation while correctly noting mutable mux state.

old_problem: I2C-6-to-bus5 mapping, mux0x71 port2 semantics, expected downstream UPHY1 replies, force-access ownership, combined-bit behavior, measurable PASS criteria and exact restoration are absent; prior reviews added unsupported physical probing.
disposition_reason: ED-03 permits a standard BMC I2C draft but OEM bus/mux/downstream mappings cannot be guessed. The source supports a hybrid functional transaction, not mandatory solder/probe evidence. Execution remains Pending until PID1114953 supplies the target/oracle and safe restoration, but it is not fundamentally BLOCKED.
decision_basis: Read row123/history2514 and kept first-PG548 mux0x71 distinct from row124 second-PG548 mux0x75.
Preserved BMC login, bus5, mux0x71, value0x04, port2, UPHY1 and PID1114953.
Rejected invented physical probing, soldering and mandatory photos as source coverage.
Required downstream transaction evidence, exclusive mux ownership and exact original-byte restoration.
No bus scan, forced read/write, mux change, BMC reset, physical probe or DUT action occurred.

test_case.test_name: First PG548 BMC I2C-6 to UPHY1 functional path
test_case.purpose: Verify the first-PG548 management path from logical BMC I2C-6 through Linux bus5 mux0x71 port2 to PID1114953-defined UPHY1 devices, then restore the exact prior mux state without disrupting other channels.
required_package: PID1114953 topology and expected downstream address/register/reply matrix
Proof logical BMC I2C-6 maps to Linux/i2c-tools bus5
Mux0x71 register/port2 definition,0x04 semantics and allowed combined bits
Mux owner/driver plus exclusive raw-access window
Exact downstream reads, timeout/NACK/error rules, original-state restore and BMC recovery
test_case.test_command: After approval, record BMC/bus ownership and original mux byte with the literal read; select port2 using the approved0x04 or masked equivalent; verify readback; issue only the PID-defined bounded downstream UPHY1 reads; capture errors; restore the exact original byte and revalidate management services.
test_case.expected_result: The authoritative first-PG548 downstream addresses return the signed replies within timeout through mux0x71 port2, no arbitration/stuck-bus/service impact occurs, and mux readback plus all management/device health return exactly to the pre-test state.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires proven controller mapping, approved select semantics, expected downstream responses and exact restoration. Mux ACK alone, blind scan, NACK/timeout/arbitration loss, unrelated channel impact, wrong readback or incomplete restore fails; photos/probing are not required absent a separate decision.
safety_gate: BMC/platform-management ownership, independent recovery and authoritative topology.
No raw/force access while a driver, daemon or other test owns mux0x71.
Capture original byte; do not overwrite other required bits by assumption.
One bounded select/read sequence; abort on bus or management degradation and restore immediately.
expected_evidence: BMC/i2c-tools identity, ownership/concurrency and health baseline
Original mux byte, exact read/select and approved readback interpretation
Expected-versus-observed downstream transaction matrix with timestamps/status
Bus/kernel/daemon logs and no unrelated impact
Exact restoration/readback, device/service health and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Restore the exact recorded mux byte using the approved BMC path, verify all PID-listed devices and management services, and invoke independent BMC recovery only if the bus remains stuck. Do not scan blindly, reset automatically or leave port selection changed.
